statements.t: The Company’s BESS is a validated chemistry with accessible non-precious earth components in a durable design that is intended to deliver results in even the most extreme temperatures and conditions.
We believe the Z3 battery will transform how utility, industrial and commercial customers store power.
The Company’s current and target customers include utilities, project developers, independent power producers, C&I companies and government contracts.
The Company expects DawnOS to be an integral component of its product portfolio going forward, supporting enhanced efficiency, safety and overall system performance.
The Company expects Indensity to be an integral component of its product portfolio going forward.

In addition, the Company benefits from legislative incentives, including the Inflation Reduction Act and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA"), which provide production tax credits (“PTC”) for domestically manufactured battery components, as well as tax credits available to customers for projects that satisfy domestic content requirements.

The Company also intends to continue working with a consortium of community organizations, universities and supply chain partners to pursue available funding opportunities under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law of 2021.

Under the agreement, Eos will deploy WATTMORE's platform on select customer projects, expanding the controls ecosystem for the Company's energy storage solutions and supporting streamlined project deployment.

Management believes the integrated platform will simplify project deployment, reduce implementation complexity and enhance the overall customer value proposition by offering a more comprehensive energy storage solution.
In August 2026, the Company announced plans to consolidate its battery manufacturing operations at its Thorn Hill facility in Warrendale, Pennsylvania.

The Thorn Hill facility is expected to provide approximately 4 GWh of annual nameplate manufacturing capacity when both production lines are fully operational, supporting the Company's anticipated growth and expansion of customer deployments.
Management believes the consolidation will improve manufacturing efficiency by reducing material handling and streamlining production workflows.
Upon completion of the transition, the Company expects to achieve conversion cost reductions, with benefits anticipated to begin in 2027.
The Company currently expects to complete the transition without impacting customer delivery commitments.
The Company expects revenues to increase as it scales production to meet customer demand.
The Company's revenue profile is influenced by the timing of project deployments.
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, approximately 83% of the Company’s revenue was attributable to deliveries associated with related party projects.
The Company expects revenue concentration to vary from period to period as individual projects advance through their delivery schedules.
We expect the Company's revenue mix to align generally with the composition of its backlog and the timing of project deliveries.
As the cost structure initiatives are implemented and operational efficiencies continue to improve, management expects further gross margin improvement in future periods.
The Company has invested ahead of expected growth by building the team, systems and capabilities required to support a significantly larger revenue base.
As revenue grows, management expects SG&A expenses to grow at a slower pace than revenue, allowing SG&A to become a smaller percentage of revenue over time.
The Company has historically relied on outside capital to fund its cost structure and expects this reliance to continue for the foreseeable future until the Company reaches profitability.
Through September 30, 2026, under the DOE Loan Facility, the Company drew down approximately $178.0 million for the eligible project costs that the Company had incurred.
The Company expects capital expenditures and working capital requirements to increase as it seeks to execute its growth strategy.
Critical accounting estimates are those estimates that involve a significant level of estimation uncertainty and could have a material impact on our financial condition or results of operations.
